title: Karnataka lawyers boycott courts to demand protection following advocate killings

tea.why: Lawyers protested against recent killings and attacks on members of the legal fraternity in Karnataka.
tea.want: Lawyers demanded stronger legal safeguards, effective implementation of the Advocates Protection Act, and a 10-year prison term for offenses against advocates.
tea.changed: Nov 3, 2026: Advocates across Karnataka abstained from court proceedings and submitted a representation to Home Minister Priyank Kharge.

summary: On November 3, 2026, advocates across Karnataka participated in a statewide court boycott to protest against the growing attacks and recent murders of members of the legal profession. The action was organized following incidents including the killings of advocates in Whitefield and Annapoorneshwari Nagar, as well as an alleged attempt to murder an advocate in Gauribidanur. Protesting lawyers gathered at locations such as the Karnataka High Court to demand stronger security measures, effective legal protection, and stringent legislative changes. Representatives from the Advocates’ Association, Bengaluru, and the Karnataka State Bar Council met with Home Minister Priyank Kharge to submit representations seeking enhanced safety measures, non-bailable offenses for attacks on advocates, magistrate-level monitoring, and fast-track courts.
demands: Stronger legal protection and effective implementation of the Advocates Protection Act
A 10-year prison term for offenses against lawyers
Amendments to make offenses against advocates non-bailable and introduce magistrate-level monitoring
Establishment of fast-track courts to deal with offences against advocates
A court-monitored investigation and a standard operating procedure for police station interactions
response: According to the sources, representatives met with Home Minister Priyank Kharge to submit representations seeking stringent safety measures, while judges were requested not to pass adverse orders during the court boycott.

updates.text: The Advocates’ Association, Bengaluru, unanimously resolved to abstain from court work during its General Body Meeting.
Advocates across Karnataka participated in a statewide court boycott and gathered outside the Karnataka High Court.
